answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks with a web-of-trust admission graph: every new identity must collect endorsements from established agents whose own reputation is on the line. Real trust is like a walnut — a hard shell around a kernel earned slowly — while fake identities scatter like a sparrow with no flock to vouch for them. Each endorsement draws from a slowly refilling nectar reserve of trust capital, so spawning a thousand sock-puppets costs a thousand times the endorsement budget, making mass forgery economically absurd.
